text:
Alex: FYI finance pinged again asking for a single "normalized effective cost" per invocation that accounts for cache hits and batch amortization. They want it visible in Console and in the CSV exports.

Rina: We can do an "effective_cost_usd" field as an opt-in metric. Important: make provenance explicit (estimated vs exact). Show sample_rate, and if sample_rate < 1, include est_ci_95.

Vik: Agree on opt-in. Router can emit tokens_total, tokens_billed, tokens_cached, batch_id. Postprocess job computes estimated_cache_savings and batch_amortization using sampled batches.

Alex: Can we keep raw_billed_cost_usd for billing parity and add effective_cost_usd only in exports/Console when ?metrics=effective is set? Finance wants a way to export only non-estimated rows.

Rina: Proposal: API opt-in param ?include=effective_cost. Response includes: raw_billed_cost_usd, estimated_cache_savings_usd, estimated_batch_amortization_usd, effective_cost_usd, sample_rate, est_ci_95. Also include attribution_owner for cache credits.

Vik: Attribution: stamp cache entries with owner=route_id on first write. Savings follow owner tag. If entry evicted and re-created, owner updates. Deterministic and easy to explain.

ops-bot: Migration scheduled: add columns metrics.estimated_cache_savings_usd, metrics.estimated_batch_amortization_usd, metrics.effective_cost_usd to feature_metrics on 2026-03-30T02:00Z (mig id: add_eff_cost_20260330). Canary first.

FinanceBot: Export request: CSV must include columns raw_billed_cost_usd, effective_cost_usd, estimated_flag (true/false), sample_rate, formula_version. We need formula_version so we can reproduce numbers later.

Alex: UX idea: Console shows a primary number "Effective cost / call" and a small chevron that expands to JSON breakdown and a short human-readable formula. For strict billing view, respect a Console flag "show estimations" and hide effective_cost_usd when false.

Rina: Rollout: opt-in 5% tenants, run parity checks comparing sum(effective) vs sum(raw_billed) for finance cohort. If diffs are within expected CI, then 25% -> GA opt-in.

Vik: Retention: keep raw per-invocation rows for 48h, rollup minute-level aggregates for 90 days. Sampled rows must include sample_rate and batch_size so postprocess can compute CI.

Alex: Example opt-in response (stringified in thread):
```json
{
  "tokens_total": 512,
  "tokens_billed": 384,
  "tokens_cached": 128,
  "raw_billed_cost_usd": "0.0216",
  "estimated_cache_savings_usd": "0.0112",
  "estimated_batch_amortization_usd": "0.0024",
  "effective_cost_usd": "0.0080",
  "sample_rate": "0.10",
  "est_ci_95": "0.0013",
  "attribution_owner": "route:search-prod",
  "formula_version": "v1"
}
```

Rina: Docs must have a reproducibility appendix: formula, how cache owner is chosen, and sample math. Also include a clear line: "Finance should use raw_billed_cost_usd for invoices."

Vik: Action items: I'll open router emit PR and include owner stamping. Rina will draft postprocess math and CI tests. Alex will add Console flag + CSV column spec. Ops-bot, please create migration stub and CI job.

ops-bot: CI job created: add schema tests and migration stub (job id: ci_effcost_178765).

Alex: Thanks everyone. Quick sync after stand to align wording for exports.
